evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Observation unit is the interview/field encounter as reported by the interviewer; the referent is field-side approach by community and/or party representatives, a factual-contact record rather than respondent opinion.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Act is interviewer self-report of felt threat during the interview; the subject who felt threatened is interviewer-as-asker, so the item records field safety conditions, not respondent attitudes.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Narrows Q106D from felt threat to physical threat occurrence; the two form a general/embodied pair with distinct predicates, so agreement on one does not entail the other.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened
physically threatened

claims.text: The pair separates subjective felt threat from physical threat; treating the physical item as a stricter variant of the felt item presumes reporting consistency not established by metadata.

evidence.quote: honest, in between, or misleading?

claims.text: Three-point interviewer judgment of respondent candour across the interview; response act is interviewer appraisal of another person, not a self-report of honesty.

evidence.quote: honest, in between

claims.text: The scale is directional around a midpoint glossed 'in between'; 'misleading' is a negative pole, so codes 1 and 3 are opposite judgments and 2 is the explicit neutral.

evidence.quote: must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: Forced-choice between presidential exemption from laws/courts (Statement 1) and unconditional legal submission (Statement 2); 1-4 express direction and intensity, 5 expresses rejection of both.

evidence.quote: It is legitimate for the armed forces to take control of government

claims.text: Forced-choice on military intervention in politics; unlike Q28 no not-asked code appears, so a country can still field the item while Q28 may be suppressed.

evidence.quote: making sure that, once elected, [members of Parliament] do their jobs
making sure that, once elected, the [president] does [his] job

claims.text: Shared nominal oversight-partner basket applied to two different officeholders; the parallel stems permit within-respondent comparison of who is named accountable for MPs versus the president.

evidence.quote: Not asked in Burkina Faso after 4th of October
Not asked in the country

claims.text: Scope exception differs by field: only Q48A carries a country-time-specific suppression code (93), while both carry the generic not-asked code (94), so cross-field comparison must respect wave/country availability.

evidence.quote: criticized, called names, or harassed

claims.text: Hypothetical likelihood about third-party community reaction to a woman running for office; referent is anticipated social sanction, not an observed event.

evidence.quote: doing more than they are doing now

claims.text: Normative direction-and-amount judgment about government effort on women's rights and equality; 1-2 favor less, 3 is the explicit status-quo amount, 4-5 favor more.

evidence.quote: which of the following issues

claims.text: Single-choice prioritization among named women's-rights issues, plus a substantive none/no-issue option (0) and catch-all other (6); the act is ranking, not endorsement of a policy.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Agreement that a specific emergency measure limiting freedoms is justified; the act is normative justification of coercion under a health emergency, not reporting of whether it occurred.

evidence.quote: Not applicable (COV1=0, 8 or 9)

claims.text: Contains a routing-dependent not-applicable code (97) keyed to a COVID screening item, so the eligible denominator is conditional and the item is not a full-sample opinion.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Respondent belief about the commissioning actor behind fieldwork; the act is attribution of institutional sponsorship, including coded possibilities of party, government, international organization, or God.

evidence.quote: “Afrobarometer" or national partner

claims.text: Code 1 merges the survey brand and national partner into one attribution, so the field cannot distinguish identification of the brand from identification of a local implementing partner.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Records consent-in-principle for future recontact, a disposition rather than past behaviour; code 7 marks ineligibility due to lacking a mobile number rather than refusal.

evidence.quote: does not have a mobile phone number

claims.text: The follow-up register is conditioned on phone possession, so the eligible base for willingness excludes those without a mobile number and the code is a structural eligibility state, not a negative answer.

evidence.quote: community and/or political party representatives
feel threatened
physically threatened

claims.text: Together the trio records field-encounter conditions: outsider approach, felt threat, physical threat, all interviewer-reported and anchored to the interview occasion.

holds.missing: Actual interviewer training, mode (face-to-face vs phone) and supervision rules governing these items
holds.why: Without field protocol we cannot establish who is authorized to answer, how the interviewer distinguishes an approach from harassment, or whether the three threat items share a routing

holds.missing: Country-specific fielding agency names and branding used in R9
holds.why: Code 1 merges brand and partner, so belief attribution cannot be decomposed without knowing the local implementing institution

holds.missing: Exact definition and distribution of the COV1 screening variable
holds.why: The 97 route conditions eligibility on a variable not supplied, so the effective denominator cannot be determined from this packet

holds.missing: Follow-up survey consent and data-protection procedure
holds.why: Willingness cannot be interpreted as actual recontact feasibility without the recontact protocol

inquiries.question: Among interviews where representatives approached the field team, how do felt-threat and physical-threat reports distribute, and do the two threat items diverge?
inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.alternatives: A: approach co-occurs with elevated threat reporting (contact as risk signal); B: approach occurs with near-zero threat reports (approach as benign gatekeeping). Payoff: distinguishes external interference from routinized local liaison; divergence between felt and physical threat tests whether 'felt' adds a distinct safety layer.
inquiries.ceiling: Interviewer-reported only; no respondent self-report; eligibility limited to interviewed cases; cannot establish causal direction or actual intimidation. Route/design/role/ancestry must be qualified before any computation.

inquiries.question: Does the named oversight partner for MPs (Q48A) track the named oversight partner for the president (Q48B) within the same respondent?
inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.alternatives: A: consistent hierarchical attribution (same actor blamed for both offices); B: split attribution (different actors for legislature vs executive). Payoff: reveals whether accountability is office-differentiated or a generic orientation; matters for interpreting 'the voters' selection as civic rather than institutional.
inquiries.ceiling: Both fields must be asked-eligible in the same country-wave; Q48A's 93 route excludes some Burkina Faso post-4-October cases. Nominal, one-choice; no inference to actual oversight behaviour. Candidate only; roles unqualified.

inquiries.question: Do those wanting more government action on women's rights (Q51A 4-5) name a different top-priority issue (Q51B) than those satisfied with the current amount?
inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.alternatives: A: demand-more respondents concentrate on structural issues (education, workplace); B: they concentrate on violence or representation. Payoff: tests whether 'more action' is a diffuse stance or tied to a specific grievance; a satisfied group naming no issue supports the diffuse reading.
inquiries.ceiling: Single top-choice loses salience ranks; codes 0 and 6 blur abstention and other. Both nominal/ordinal; no distribution asserted. Candidate only; independence of roles must be qualified.

inquiries.question: Is acceptance of police/security enforcement of health mandates associated with rejection of military political intervention?
inquiries.route: S04/I03 catalog joint then R14–16 if independently qualified roles and selected inquiry; candidate only
inquiries.alternatives: A: coherent anti-coercion orientation (reject both); B: selective acceptance (emergency enforcement tolerated while military rule rejected), indicating context-conditioned rather than principled restraint. Payoff: separates situational justification from general civilian-supremacy commitment.
inquiries.ceiling: Q63B applies only to COV1-eligible respondents, shrinking the denominator; Q29B forced-choice scales differ from Q63B agree/disagree, so comparison is scale-asymmetric. Candidate only.

inquiries.question: Does attributing fieldwork to Afrobarometer/partner (Q97 code 1) or to government (Q97 code 8) associate with willingness to be recontacted (Q98A)?
inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.
inquiries.alternatives: A: correct brand attribution accompanies higher willingness; B: government attribution accompanies higher willingness (authority effect). Payoff: tests whether sponsorship belief shapes future cooperation; code 1's merge of brand and partner limits attribution precision.
inquiries.ceiling: Q98A eligibility excludes phone-less respondents (code 7); Q97 nonresponse codes 98/99 must be handled. No causal claim possible; observed association only, candidate route qualification required.

nominations.reason: Presence of listeners conditions whether interviewer threat and candour items are answered truthfully; retrieval enables joint field-condition analysis with Q106C-Q106E.
Interviewer verbatim comment could contextualize threat and approach reports without interpretation before exact retrieval.
Respondent gender would allow checking whether threat/candour judgments and women's-rights items differ by respondent gender; locator only.
Rural/urban PSU context would contextualize approach by community/party representatives; locator only, no domain asserted.

response.instruction: Return one JSON object with exactly the response_contract keys. All claims cite literal evidence. O/M must cover every selected field in claims. D/M must supply every selected field and all literal answer codes (small pilot only). Other stages must return empty answer_notes. I/S/M may propose inquiries. R/M may nominate locator-only context. Prior claims are revisable; challenge exact stage-prefixed ID and retain original. No forced output counts other than coverage. Do not cite any field not in supplied source_packet except a locator nomination. All stages may return holds. No automatic calls or permissions.
response.intellectual_resources: Understand, differentiate, inherit, qualify, interrelate, conserve (§5-J). Preserve positive answer-level distinctions and exact scope. Add sparse inquiry recipes grounded in actual items; state which alternative outcomes matter, role/ancestry/risk/observation requirements and first-reader ceiling. No universal taxonomy. Context is read-only. Use economical shared notes, avoid repeating settled distinctions; expend deeper reasoning where warranted. Preserve meaningful special states and distinct local inquiry families. No invented person type, counts, causal conclusions or source grants.
